verdict.rationale: Ente's own llms.txt states that its apps and server are open source, a community commenter thanks Ente for releasing Auth as open source, and the docs link to the public github.com/ente/ente repository. Together these show the client code handling seeds is publicly inspectable. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs on the client source repos and licensing, evidence of independent security audits or actual community code review of the seed-handling code.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: Ente's apps and server are open source
This looks quite nice, thank you for releasing it open source
You can use [Ente's CLI](https://github.com/ente/ente/tree/main/cli#readme) to automatically backup your Auth codes.
